suggestions.label: honored hero cremation with precious container and companion burial
suggestions.rationale: Heroic funerary treatment and companion burial fit the mourning/hero death complex better than a general afterlife journey.
suggestions.cautions: Could also index under sacrifice or sacred_treasures if the companion burial or precious container is ritually central.

suggestions.label: human-animal identity through transferred soul
suggestions.rationale: A transferred soul producing human-animal identity is a form of identity/body transformation across species boundaries.
suggestions.cautions: If the source concerns reincarnation, soul-loss, or animist ontology rather than form-change, human review may prefer a soul-specific candidate.

suggestions.label: human interruption of divine rite prevents immortality
suggestions.rationale: The motif turns on a failed passage from mortality toward immortality or transformed life.
suggestions.cautions: May belong under initiation if the interrupted rite is a status ordeal; preserve failed-immortality detail.

suggestions.label: human mariner beholds dancing sea spirits
suggestions.rationale: A human witness encountering sea spirits is a manifestation of nonordinary divine or spirit presence.
suggestions.cautions: Could be an otherworld/sea encounter rather than a theophany; source context is needed to know whether it is revelatory, decorative, or narrative setting.

suggestions.label: Hunting and restoring a lost soul
suggestions.rationale: The active retrieval and restoration of a lost soul is a recurring healing/death-boundary pattern not well captured by descent or resurrection alone.
suggestions.cautions: Needs review for shamanic or culturally specific framing; avoid flattening distinct healing rites into generic resurrection.

suggested_new_group.label: Soul Loss and Restoration
suggested_new_group.description: A soul, life-force, or vital double is lost, stolen, wandering, or displaced and must be found, hunted, recalled, or ritually restored to heal or revive a person.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing groups cover descent, resurrection, and transformation, but not the healing function of retrieving a displaced soul without full death or underworld travel.

suggestions.label: ideal realized in death and misery
suggestions.rationale: The label is abstract and may describe a philosophical interpretation rather than a stable narrative motif.
suggestions.cautions: Needs passage evidence; could relate to lament, sacrifice, tragic recognition, or a commentary artifact.

suggestions.label: Ignored warning leads to heroic death
suggestions.suggested_group_label: Death Attributed to Fate or Destiny
suggestions.rationale: A warning ignored before heroic death often marks an inescapable destined death or doomed heroic path.
suggestions.cautions: If emphasis is moral failure rather than fate, divine_judgment or pride_and_downfall may be better.

suggestions.label: Illness or misfortune attributed to harmful spirits and treated by expulsion
suggestions.rationale: Spirit-caused affliction treated by expulsion is a distinct healing/exorcistic pattern not covered by judgment or sacrifice alone.
suggestions.cautions: Culturally sensitive; review terminology against source tradition and avoid assuming demonology where the source uses other spirit categories.

suggested_new_group.label: Spirit Affliction and Expulsion
suggested_new_group.description: Illness, misfortune, possession, or disorder is attributed to harmful spirits, intrusive forces, or nonhuman agents and treated through expulsion, cleansing, appeasement, or ritual removal.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing groups cover sacred exchange, sacrifice, and divine action, but not the diagnostic and healing structure of affliction by spirits and ritual expulsion.

suggestions.label: immanent spirit becoming external deity
suggestions.rationale: The label appears theoretical or comparative and may describe a religious-development claim rather than a motif in a passage.
suggestions.cautions: Review for whether this is source evidence, scholarly commentary, or an ontology category; avoid taxonomy placement based on theory alone.

suggestions.label: Immortal soul as source of motion
suggestions.rationale: This is likely a philosophical doctrine about soul rather than a narrative or ritual motif.
suggestions.cautions: May be better excluded as doctrinal commentary unless the passage uses it as a recurring mythic image or cosmological pattern.

suggestions.label: Immortality and unity of the created state

suggestions.label: immortality experienced as lamentation
suggestions.rationale: The emphasis is on grief or tragic recognition associated with deathlessness rather than resurrection or return.
suggestions.cautions: If the passage centers on the curse or mechanics of immortality, a separate immortality motif may be needed.

suggestions.label: immortality substance withheld and destroyed
suggestions.rationale: An object or substance confers immortality and is withheld or destroyed, fitting power-object logic.
suggestions.cautions: Could also relate to forbidden_knowledge or death_and_transformation if the passage stresses denied access to deathlessness.

suggestions.label: Immortality without eternal youth
suggestions.rationale: This is a recurring mythic pattern where deathlessness is separated from youth or renewal, not covered well by resurrection or death-rebirth.
suggestions.cautions: Single occurrence in this audit; promote only if additional examples recur across traditions.

suggested_new_group.label: Immortality Without Renewal
suggested_new_group.description: Deathlessness, extended life, or escape from death becomes incomplete, burdensome, or defective because youth, vitality, release, or transformation is absent.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing death_and_transformation groups emphasize death, return, or renewal; this motif specifically concerns failed or incomplete immortality.

suggestions.label: Impermanence of glory after a great teacher’s death
suggestions.rationale: The label frames reflection after death as tragic recognition of impermanence and loss.
suggestions.cautions: May be a doctrinal teaching on impermanence rather than a narrative motif; consider sacred_knowledge if didactic context dominates.

suggestions.label: indestructible immortal soul
suggestions.rationale: This is likely a doctrinal claim about the soul rather than a narrative motif; context is needed.
suggestions.cautions: Could support afterlife_passage, sacred_knowledge, or a new soul/immortality group, but should not be forced into resurrection.

suggestions.label: inner division of the soul
suggestions.rationale: The divided soul expresses internal opposition or complementarity rather than a death journey itself.
suggestions.cautions: If treated as psychology or ethics in the source, sacred_knowledge or an inner_life group may fit better.

suggestions.label: intermediary spirits carry prayers and divine gifts
suggestions.rationale: Intermediary spirits mediate traffic between human and divine realms through prayers and gifts.
suggestions.cautions: If ritual exchange is central, also review under sacred_exchange; if psychopompic, review under afterlife_passage.

suggestions.label: intoxication as spirit possession or inspiration
suggestions.rationale: Intoxication functions as altered perception, possession, or inspired access to nonordinary knowledge.
suggestions.cautions: Comparative label may be broad; if ritual mechanics dominate, consider sacred_exchange or initiation.

suggestions.label: Invulnerability through externalized soul
suggestions.rationale: This is a distinct and widely recognizable tale motif: life or vulnerability is stored outside the body.
suggestions.cautions: Do not collapse into generic immortality; the key function is externalized life as source of invulnerability and vulnerability.

suggested_new_group.label: External Soul and Hidden Life
suggested_new_group.description: A being's life, soul, death, or vulnerability is stored outside the body in an object, animal, place, or nested container, making the being invulnerable until it is found or destroyed.
suggested_new_group.reason_existing_groups_insufficient: Existing groups cover death, transformation, and power objects, but not the specific narrative structure of life externalized outside the body.
